newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Spanish stocks shoot to record high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Spanish stocks shoot to record high.

text.p: The Spanish stock market shot to a record high on Tuesday, powered by interest in the electricity sector, a higher dollar and sharp gains on Wall Street.
The government's announcement on Monday of an aggressive privatisation plan for next year also helped spur the IBEX index to a record high of 4,324.88 in afternoon trade -- up 58.81 on the day.

"The market has been fearing much tougher regulations in the utility sector," said Luis Broto, salesman at BZW in Madrid. "The latest statements of the government indicate it is not going to be much different."
Broto said recent government statements pointed to a slower phasing out of regulations in the utility sector, relieving fears of a quick move to increased competition.
"It will take five years to be ready for more competition. The fact it will remain a regulated sector has brought a lot of confidence to investors," Broto added.
The government said on Monday it would delay the sale of its 66 percent stake in Spain's largest electrical group, Endesa, which helped calm market jitters about increased competition.
Philippe Sardet, director of Credit Lyonnais Securities Espana, reported good buying interest from international investors and European portfolio managers, concentrated in electricity stocks.
"There is also interest in some special companies related to the dollar's rise," Sardet added, citing stainless steel maker Acerinox.
The banking sector also attracted buyers' interest amid a favourable outlook for Spanish interest rates.
The advance on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones industrial average has shot well above 6,000, also whetted appetites for Spanish stocks, dealers said.
The planned privatisations in 1997 will increase liquidity in the market, Sardet said.
"This proves to investors the government is ready to let the market go up and to increase the free float of the companies," he said.

Dealers said the stock market was now catching up with a stunning bond market rally in recent months, driven by government promises of an austere budget that would put Spain on track to qualify for European Monetary Union in 1999.
"I am convinced the market will increase its price-earnings ratio in the coming six months," Sardet said.
Among the top performers in the market on Tuesday were Endesa, with an almost three percent gain, Acerinox, up more than three percent, and Gas Natural, up almost two percent.
